### Day 76: 2 Samuel 24:1–10
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-76-2-samuel-24-110.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 24:1
Points:
- Difficult biblical accounts can cause believers to question God's kindness if not approached carefully.
- Believers should remember that God's understanding exceeds human comprehension and He owes no explanations.
- When troubled by what is unexplained in Scripture, peace comes from trusting what God has already revealed about Himself.
- Scripture elsewhere affirms that God cannot be tempted by evil nor does He entice anyone to sin.
- God permitted Satan to incite the census to expose the hidden condition of David's heart.

### Bible Pathways 04/20/2003
Author: Bible Pathways
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-04-or-20-or-2003-1195307.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 24:1
Points:
- David's desire to number his troops was rooted in self-glorifying pride rather than an actual military threat.
- Satan readily exploits seasons of victory and achievement to tempt believers with sinful self-reliance.
- God's supreme sovereignty permits individuals to follow their own stubborn desires without God being the author of sin.
- The census neglected the Mosaic command requiring a ransom payment when registering Israel's men.
- David's failure serves as a sobering warning to pray for hearts aligned with God's pleasing will.
